exposure: refusal of attempted vaginal delivery and insistence of the woman for delivery through CS
presence of pain in the region of the surgical cicatrix
cohort: The study included 467 deliveries through Caesarean section, covering women of various ages, parity, and pregnancy types.
finding: The leading indication for surgical intervention in this study was the presence of an already performed CS, often accompanied by other factors like low pelvic score, established labour, or pain in the surgical cicatrix.
mod_finding: 32 pregnant women stated a refusal of attempted vaginal delivery and insistence on CS, who showed higher education levels but no statistically significant difference in postoperative stay compared to the rest of the cohort.
